messages:
maya: FYI I landed xglm-13b (8-bit quant) to dedicated yesterday and we are seeing two issues in production: higher hallucination rate on multi-turn QA and p95 latency ~2x compared to our fp16 baseline. Can reproduce locally on a dev box. Opening thread to triage.

sam: Do you have a quick repro prompt and the exact quant config? dynamic/static, per-channel?

maya: repro: small QA set (10 prompts) I pushed to /tmp/xglm_repro.json. Quant was post-training static int8 per-tensor (used our quantize_tool v0.9) — config: --mode static --bits 8 --per_channel false.

liam: Any differences in kernel selection or runtime flags vs the fp16 rollout? Was the serving runtime updated at the same time?

maya: We did roll runtime 2 hours before model -- but the same runtime was rolled to other models without regressions. Kernel selection log shows fallback to slower aten kernels for some attention ops with this quantized artifact.

anjali: Possible numerical instability from per-tensor quantization. For LMs with heavy attention patterns, per-channel quant is often safer. Can you re-quant with --per_channel true and run the eval harness?

maya: running that now locally. Also saw weird token-level probabilities: many low-prob tokens but still sampled — smells like logit scaling bug after dequant step.

sam: Can you paste the eval run output (ppl/accuracy/delta vs fp16) and the exact command you used to serve?

maya: eval command: ``python eval_harness.py --model /models/xglm-13b/quant8_static.pt --eval datasets/qa_small.json --batch 1 --seed 42`` Results: fp16 baseline acc 0.78 ppl 12.1; quant8_static acc 0.63 ppl 25.7. per_channel quant in progress.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3189. Notifying eng-sre.

liam: If ppls diverge that much it's more than just a kernel perf issue — likely numeric distortion. Two parallel actions: 1) rollback model to fp16 on dedicated pool, 2) re-quant with per-channel and different clipping params. Who can do rollback?

maya: I'll request rollback now for the dedicated deployment and pin traffic to the fp16 variant.

anjali: For re-quant I'd try these experiments: (a) per-channel int8, (b) symmetric vs asymmetric quant, (c) calibrate with longer calibration set (10k steps), (d) try 4-bit QAT fallback if 8-bit keeps failing. Also add a small eval of token-prob distributions vs fp16 (KL divergence).

sam: Also check kv-cache implementation: if the cached keys/values are quantized incorrectly or stored in lower precision, it can blow up cumulative error across turns. Add a unit test that runs 8-turn chat and compares logits to fp16 after each turn.

maya: Good call. I inspected kv dumps — they looked same shape but SNR lower. I'll add the unit test.

liam: Perf angle: the aten fallback for some fused attention kernels explains the p95 spike. If per-channel fixes numeric, we may still need a kernel patch to avoid fallback on this shape. File a bug with eng-runtime with attached kernel traces and machine profile.

maya: Created runtime bug: RT-4567, attached kernel traces and repro.

anjali: For immediate mitigation, after rollback we should add a bring-up checklist item: mandatory per-channel quant attempt + calibration > 1k examples + KL<0.05 vs fp16 before canary. Also add the kv-cache 8-turn test as a gating CI test.

sam: Agree. I'll add checklist PR to eng-ml docs: 1) baseline fp16 eval, 2) quant per-channel try, 3) numeric checks (KL/ppl), 4) kv-cache multi-turn unit, 5) perf smoke (p50/p95 within 1.4x), 6) runtime kernel trace sanity.

maya: After rollback: traffic pinned and alert quieted. Taking ownership of re-quant experiments. ETA EOD for per-channel run and eval.

liam: I can help with perf traces and open a follow-up to optimize fused attention to avoid aten fallback — will loop in @eng-runtime.

anjali: If per-channel doesn't cut it, try per-channel calibration + symmetric quant + clip to 99.9 percentile. Also try running our quantization with the new kernel-selection flag that avoids an unsafe fusion until we patch runtime.

maya: Update: per-channel run complete, acc 0.76 ppl 13.4, KL to fp16 ~0.028. p95 improved but still ~1.6x. Uploading logs to /shared/ml/onboard/xglm-13b/quant_runs/1771234567/.

sam: That's promising. Let's hold a short canary today with 5% traffic after runtime kernel fix is staged. If p95 still >1.5x we revert. Also run the regression eval suite to make sure no other dims break.

infra-bot: Canary scheduled: CANARY-877 for xglm-13b (5% traffic) at 19:30 UTC.

maya: Assigning action items: maya -> complete kv-cache unit test + re-quant tuning; sam -> PR checklist; liam -> eng-runtime bug triage; anjali -> expand calibration harness. Will update this thread with links.

sam: Thanks all. Documenting post-launch checklist changes under eng-ml/processes/onboarding.md after this stabilizes. :thumbsup:
